name: Mathematics
question: What exact structure does this subject have, and which proved results apply once their conditions are met?
breaks: a hypothesis of the theorem fails
the model drops a feature that matters
rules_of_thumb: State the problem in its most general true form, then specialise
Ask whether the problem is really about a graph, a group, a space or a distribution
collisions: Every field cites MA theorems by ID; MA owns the proof, the other field owns the use
Modelling (MA.B.C4) meets PH, EC, BI and CS

name: Foundations
question: What may be assumed, what can be decided, and can the problem be stated in a formal language?
look_for: categorical structure: objects, maps, universal properties
find_out: Formalise in a proof assistant (Lean, Coq)
Reduce to a known decidable or undecidable problem
breaks: hidden use of choice or infinity
a reduction that is not effective
rules_of_thumb: If a problem resists, ask whether it is independent of the axioms
Category theory finds the same pattern in different fields

name: Structure
question: What operations, orders and number patterns does the problem have, and what algebra classifies them?
breaks: structure assumed commutative or linear when it is not
rules_of_thumb: Representation theory turns symmetry into linear algebra
Many hard problems become easy as graph problems
collisions: Cryptography (CS.O.A5) rests on number theory hardness assumptions

name: Space
question: What shape, nearness or dimension does the problem live in, and what does that shape force?
look_for: manifold structure of the solution set
rules_of_thumb: Ask what is preserved under deformation
Fixed-point theorems prove existence without construction
collisions: Physics (PH.O.A3) uses differential geometry; data analysis uses topology

name: Change and the continuum
question: How do quantities change, what equations govern them, and do solutions exist, stay unique and stay bounded?
rules_of_thumb: Fourier analysis turns convolution into multiplication
collisions: PH, EN and EC models are A4 equations in use

name: Chance
question: Where is uncertainty, what distribution describes it, and what can be inferred from data?
look_for: limit laws (law of large numbers, central limit)
breaks: model fitted to the same data it is tested on
rules_of_thumb: Concentration inequalities bound deviations without full distributions
Ask what is random and with respect to what
collisions: Statistics in every empirical field; causal inference (W5) builds on it
